sentences.text: The species name beloclis translates to "arrow clavicle," a reference to the triangular shape of its interclavicle bone.
Scientists currently know five specimens of this animal, including one complete skeleton with a skull and full tail, as well as a young individual.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in Peterborough, England, and later acquired by Alfred Nicholson Leeds. Charles William Andrews formally established the genus Picrocleidus in 1910.
Picrocleidus is classified as a member of the family Cryptoclididae.
It is debated whether Picrocleidus is synonymous with the genus Muraenosaurus.
This animal lived in the United Kingdom during the Middle Jurassic Callovian stage, between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
